title: Learners judge an agent by its persona
statement: Learners can take a scripted teaching agent for an adaptive one and judge it by its persona.
detail: A paper on scripted pedagogical agents, pasted into the Grade 9 unit's design chat, reports from its authors' earlier work that learners assume such agents give dynamically generated, adaptive responses even when they do not, and, citing an earlier suggestion, that learners deal with an agent through its interface and persona rather than its algorithms (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`, lines 2761-2763). Its authors recommend an expert agent to introduce new content or demonstrate a procedure in a well-defined subject, and a peer-like motivating agent for ill-structured domains and low-achieving students (lines 2753-2759). The advice on domains and low-achieving students comes from the paper's discussion, not from a comparison across them. The unit's design brief took the agent roles and their looks as hypotheses to test with its own students (line 3075).
against: The study used scripted agents with college students, and the unit's design brief adds: "Their work supports investigating different instructional functions; it does not validate three conversational agents working together." (`g9/transcript/chat-transcript.redacted.txt`, line 3075). The claim about persona is a cited suggestion, not a measured result.

evidence.quote: learners assume agents such as these are providing dynamically-generated and adaptive responses, even when they are not
learners interact with agents as represented through their interface (e.g., persona), not through their underlying algorithms.
The Expert would be appropriate to introduce new content or demonstrate a procedure within a well-defined subject area
The Motivator may be more appropriate in ill-structured domains or constructivist learning environments, where learners’ voluntary engagement is more critical than their knowledge acquisition.
Also, the Motivator may work more effectively with low achieving students, who are sometimes motivated by working with those who are of a similarly competency level
we operationalized a motivator agent with a peer-like image of a casually-dressed student in his twenties

citations.ref: Simulating instructional roles through pedagogical agents (International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education, 2005)
